title: SPHEREx Sky Diary - 3-Minute Challenge Pitch Walkthrough

steps.title: 1. Target Region & Field of View
steps.caption: Welcome to SPHEREx Sky Diary! We begin centered on SPHEREx Deep Field North (RA 269.452°, Dec +66.561°), an ultra-deep observational window surveyed every 6 months.

steps.title: 2. Multi-Epoch Time-Lapse & Blink Comparator
steps.caption: Toggling the Blink Comparator rapidly alternates between observation epochs. Stationary stars remain locked in place, while solar system objects clearly jump back and forth.

steps.title: 3. Mover Detection & Trajectory Trails
steps.caption: Our offline pipeline automatically links transient centroids across epochs into constant-velocity tracklets, plotting motion trails that indicate speed and direction.

steps.title: 4. Known Object: 1 Ceres
steps.caption: Selecting candidate SPX-MOV-0001 reveals a 91% confidence match to dwarf planet 1 Ceres, validated against the official IMCCE SkyBoT astronomical ephemeris database.

steps.title: 5. Unknown Candidate & Honest Science
steps.caption: Selecting SPX-MOV-0002 highlights an unmatched mover! Sky Diary displays an honest science notice: 'Not matched to asteroid catalogs; candidate for follow-up, not a confirmed discovery'.

steps.title: 6. 102-Channel Spectrophotometry (SED)
steps.caption: SPHEREx captures 102 spectral channels from 0.75 to 5.0 µm. The SED graph displays surface diagnostic features and provides one-click CSV export for astronomical research.

steps.title: 7. Share Findings & Embed Everywhere
steps.caption: Click Share to generate a high-res 1200x630 social card (with TEST DATA transparency), copy a direct link with all viewport parameters, or grab an iframe embed snippet.
